The ordinary-mode power fraction quantifies the share of one launched electron-cyclotron beam carried by the ordinary (O) polarization mode rather than the extraordinary (X) mode.

It is defined by the ratio

$$
f_O = \frac{P_O}{P_{\mathrm{EC}}}
$$

where $f_O$ is the ordinary-mode power fraction, $P_O$ is the launched power in the ordinary mode, and $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the total launched power of the electron-cyclotron beam.

The quantity applies to a single electron-cyclotron beam and uses launched beam power aggregated over the beam's ordinary-mode content. It excludes power from other beams and does not represent the total launched power itself. Values of $f_O=1$ and $f_O=0$ denote pure ordinary-mode and pure extraordinary-mode launch, respectively.

This power partition is distinct from [polarization ellipticity of a polarimeter beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam), which describes the shape and handedness of a polarization ellipse rather than the O-mode fraction of an electron-cyclotron beam.

copies.documentation:
MHD plasma stored energy is the global energy content assigned to the plasma by integrating its equilibrium-reconstructed total kinetic pressure over the full plasma volume. It includes thermal and fast-particle contributions rather than representing only one pressure population.

The defining relation is

$$
W_{\mathrm{MHD}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{tot}}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{MHD}}$ is the MHD plasma stored energy, $p_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total kinetic pressure determined by the equilibrium reconstruction, $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the complete plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

The quantity is the signed local ratio of the plasma bulk center-of-mass velocity parallel to the magnetic field to the magnitude of the local total magnetic-induction vector. It represents parallel plasma motion weighted by the inverse field strength.

The defining relation is

$$
\frac{v_{\parallel,\mathrm{plasma}}}{|\mathbf{B}|}

$$

where $v_{\parallel,\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma bulk velocity component parallel to the magnetic field, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the aggregate plasma center-of-mass velocity vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local total magnetic-induction vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude.

The velocity is aggregated as the center-of-mass velocity of the plasma species and is evaluated locally. It is not a species-resolved velocity or a neutral-particle velocity, and the denominator is the total field magnitude rather than a signed toroidal or poloidal field component.

The numerator is the [parallel plasma velocity](name:parallel_plasma_velocity), while the denominator is the [magnetic-field magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude); consequently, this quantity retains the numerator's flow direction while scaling it by the inverse local field strength. It is distinct from the [parallel Mach number](name:parallel_mach_number), whose denominator is the local plasma sound speed.

This coefficient specifies the strength of the limiter applied to energy transport by neutral particles occupying one selected internal state. It is a closure parameter rather than an energy flux or an energy density.

The limiter imposes the bound

$$
\lvert \mathbf{q}_E \rvert \leq \alpha_E q_{E,\max}
$$

where $\alpha_E$ is this flux-limiter coefficient, $\mathbf{q}_E$ is the energy-flux-density vector carried by the selected neutral internal state, and $q_{E,\max}$ is the prescribed maximum admissible magnitude for that energy flux.

The coefficient applies to the energy channel of neutral transport for the specified internal state. It does not sum over neutral internal states or neutral species, does not represent the energy flux itself, and has no edge-region restriction in its definition. It is distinct from the corresponding momentum limiter, such as the [neutral internal-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region), which constrains momentum rather than energy transport.

The coefficient scales the admissible energy-flux bound in the closure: increasing $\alpha_E$ permits a larger maximum energy flux relative to $q_{E,\max}$, while the coefficient itself remains a dimensionless scalar.

One millimetre equals one thousand micrometres.

dd_source.documentation: Ion temperature (averaged on charge states and ion species)

copies.documentation:
Ion average temperature is the effective kinetic temperature of the combined ion population, formed from all included ion species and their charge states at a given plasma location.

The density-weighted mean is defined by

$$
T_i = \frac{\sum_s \sum_z n_{s,z} T_{s,z}}{\sum_s \sum_z n_{s,z}}
$$

where $T_i$ is the ion average temperature, $s$ indexes the included ion species, $z$ indexes the charge states of each species, $n_{s,z}$ is the number density of that species and charge state, and $T_{s,z}$ is its temperature.

The aggregation includes all ion species and all charge states, with number-density weighting rather than an unweighted arithmetic mean. The quantity applies throughout the closed-field plasma and scrape-off layer. For radial evaluations, closed-field values use flux-surface averaging, while scrape-off-layer values use the local outboard-midplane value.

This quantity excludes neutral particles and electrons, is not a sum of temperatures or an energy density, and does not itself denote a volume, line, or spatial average. The spatial evaluation convention is distinct from the intrinsic species and charge-state aggregation.

The combined-population interpretation corresponds to [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature); [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature) additionally applies a spatial volume average.

One microsecond equals one millionth of a second.

dd_source.documentation: Source rate of thermal particle density

copies.documentation:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current direction.

The source contribution to the evolution of the counter-passing thermal particle number density is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{source}}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is this source rate, $n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged number density of counter-passing thermal particles, $\psi$ is the magnetic flux-surface label, $t$ is time, and the source subscript denotes the explicit particle-source contribution. Positive values represent net particle addition, while negative values represent net particle removal.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population in the counter-passing orbit class and is averaged over magnetic flux surfaces. It is not summed over co-passing or trapped orbit classes and excludes nonthermal particle populations. The corresponding [co-passing thermal particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) applies the same source definition to the co-passing orbit class.

The broader [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate) aggregates the orbit-population contributions, including this counter-passing component; this quantity therefore represents only the counter-passing contribution rather than the total thermal source.

The area of a rectangle equals its length times its width.
